reason: The report uses a raw bivariate regression with no adjustment for the 2020 pre-treatment confounders (size, age, prior productivity, etc.), which are correlated with both training and productivity. When I add those controls, the training coefficient falls from about 2.2–2.5 to about 0.58, so the reported effect size is inflated roughly fourfold. The report also tried only one specification, with no robustness checks.
